adjudication.rationale: Both annotations identify the same removed KeyboardInterrupt handler, the same affected method and head lines, the same low severity, and the same actionable restoration. Their taxonomy labels differ only in specificity: “error-handling-regression” is a subtype-style formulation of “error-handling,” so there is substantive taxonomy agreement.

findings.comment_usefulness_rationale: A developer-facing comment is useful and actionable because retaining the prior KeyboardInterrupt guard would preserve the advertised synchronous CTRL+C shutdown behavior independently of the parser-readiness change.

evidence_refs.description: HTTPServer.wait now loops around sleep without handling KeyboardInterrupt.
The base implementation caught KeyboardInterrupt and exited the wait loop cleanly.
The public run path advertises Ctrl+C shutdown and directly calls HTTPServer.wait.

reviewer_labels.rationale: This unrelated removal changes the documented synchronous server shutdown path: pressing Ctrl+C now lets KeyboardInterrupt escape from HTTPServer.wait and httpx.run instead of returning normally. Context-manager cleanup still runs, but normal interactive termination can now surface an exception/traceback to callers and scripts.

evidence_refs.description: HTTPServer.wait now loops around sleep without handling KeyboardInterrupt.
The base implementation caught KeyboardInterrupt and broke out of the wait loop cleanly.
The server advertises CTRL+C as its normal quit mechanism and run() directly calls server.wait().

reviewer_labels.rationale: Removing the KeyboardInterrupt handler changes the synchronous run() shutdown path: pressing CTRL+C still unwinds the server context, but KeyboardInterrupt now escapes run() and ordinarily produces an exception traceback instead of returning normally. This is an unrelated user-visible regression in the same PR, not part of the clean client-disconnect fix.

technical_evidence: HEAD src/httpx/_server.py:111-113 removes the try/except and calls sleep(1) in an infinite loop.
BASE src/httpx/_server.py:103-108 caught KeyboardInterrupt and broke from HTTPServer.wait().
HEAD src/httpx/_server.py:128-137 advertises CTRL+C as the quit mechanism and has run() call server.wait() directly.
findings.technical_rationale: The base implementation absorbed KeyboardInterrupt and returned from HTTPServer.wait(), whereas the head implementation allows it to propagate through wait() and run(). The surrounding context manager still performs cleanup during unwinding, but callers and command-line users observe changed termination behavior, potentially including an uncaught KeyboardInterrupt traceback. The frozen diff directly establishes this regression. Annotator B's base line range is inaccurate, but its described code is present at base lines 103-108 and the error does not undermine the finding.
